headline: 2026 Entry and Separate Stay Reservations
reservation: Yosemite does not require an entrance reservation in 2026; the standard entrance fee still applies. Check NPS for requirements in other years and for separate activity permits. Reservations for in-park lodging and campgrounds are managed through separate official portals and typically fill months in advance.

days.title: Introduction to the Granite Cathedral

stops.name: Tunnel View
stops.detail: Capture the classic vista of El Capitan, Half Dome, and Bridalveil Fall from this historic viewpoint.

stops.name: Mariposa Grove
stops.detail: Walk among over 500 mature giant sequoias, including the Grizzly Giant and California Tunnel Tree.

days.driving: Allow 3 to 4 hours including the Wawona Road transit; traffic may delay arrival
days.note: Access to Mariposa Grove requires a seasonal shuttle from the Welcome Center; check operations before heading to the grove.

days.title: Waterfalls and Valley Vistas

stops.name: Mist Trail
stops.detail: Climb the stone stairs to the brink of Vernal Fall for close-up views of the powerful Merced River descent.

stops.name: Lower Yosemite Fall
stops.detail: Take the easy loop trail to stand at the base of North America's tallest waterfall system.

days.driving: Use the Valley Shuttle; allow 5 to 7 hours for hiking and transit
days.note: The Mist Trail is extremely wet in spring; footwear with good traction is essential for the granite steps.

days.title: High Country and Alpine Meadows

stops.name: Glacier Point
stops.detail: Look down 3,200 feet into Yosemite Valley for an aerial perspective of the High Sierra and Half Dome.

stops.name: Olmsted Point
stops.detail: View the northern side of Half Dome and Tenaya Lake from the boulders along Tioga Road.

days.driving: Allow 5 to 6 hours round trip; these roads are seasonal and weather-dependent
days.note: Glacier Point and Tioga Roads typically open in late May or June and close with the first significant snow in autumn.

intel.title: Valley Floor Congestion
intel.text: Parking in Yosemite Valley often fills by 9 AM during peak season. Park once at Yosemite Village or Curry Village and utilize the free shuttle to move between trailheads.

intel.title: Disconnected Wilderness
intel.text: Expect very limited to no cellular service throughout the park, including the High Country. Print or download essential maps and reservation QR codes before leaving gateway towns like Oakhurst or Groveland.

intel.title: High Country Fuel
intel.text: No fuel is available in Yosemite Valley or Tuolumne Meadows. Refuel before entering the high country; check current service information for Crane Flat and Wawona before relying on either station.

intel.title: Waterfall Peak
intel.text: Waterfall volume peaks in May and June with the spring snowmelt. By late August, Yosemite Falls may be a trickle or completely dry depending on the previous winter's snowpack.

intel.title: Winter Chains
intel.text: Tire chains may be required on any park road at any time during the winter months, regardless of vehicle type. Check the current chain control status via the official park road line before entering the mountains.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Fresno Yosemite International (FAT); purchase groceries in Oakhurst before the final 90-minute climb into the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for summer, but check rental contracts for restrictions on the steep, winding mountain passes; RVs over 40 feet have restricted access to certain roads.
plan.goldenHour: Sentinel Dome provides a 360-degree sunset view, though hikers must bring headlamps for the return walk in twilight.
